entries.notes: Three edited passages. (1) l.419, Algorithm 1's loss: L = (b/2B) sum_t delta f_init(s_t) p_t(s) - E_kappa log f-hat_term. This is klwfmLossReal's form, b * int delta f_init d nu_train - int log f-hat_term d kappa, with b on the penalty and the cross-entropy unweighted, i.e. Eq. (15) (l.384) with nu_train the p_t-weighted state measure of the buffer. v1 l.395 put b on the cross-entropy. (2) l.421, 'a Monte-Carlo estimate of (15), with b >= 1 + ||d lambda/d nu_train||_inf'. The condition is hb of EGF.loss_controls_sampling_essSup: 1 + (essSup (lam.rnDeriv nu_train) nu_train).toReal <= b, the L^inf(nu_train) norm. The two other hypotheses of that theorem are presupposed by the text, not stated. hnuT (lambda << nu_train) is presupposed because v2 l.157 defines d mu/d nu only for mu << nu. hM (the essSup is finite) is presupposed because a real b cannot satisfy b >= 1 + infinity. Lean's rnDeriv exists without absolute continuity, so in Lean both have to be stated. The remaining hypotheses of the theorem come from the setting. F_init << lambda and F_init(S) = 1: Algorithm 1's input 'a source of density f_init' and Corollary 3.10's F_init(S) = 1. F_out << lambda: the model f_out*. InflowAC: l.200, nonsingular moves, C-6. kappa << lambda, a probability with finite entropy: l.377 and l.450. lambda finite: l.161. A finite loss: the bound concerns a finite L. The rendered text states no conclusion at l.421. It does not say what b >= 1 + N buys (the floor H(kappa) <= L and TV(s_tau || kappa) <= sqrt((L - H)/2) + min(1, N (L - H))), so it claims less than the Lean. 'A Monte-Carlo estimate of (15)' is not an overclaim. Eq. (15) leaves nu_train free ('for some training distribution of paths', l.386), and the first term of L is exactly b * int delta f_init d nu-hat, where nu-hat = (1/2B) sum_paths sum_t p_t delta_{s_t}. So L estimates (15) for nu_train := E[nu-hat], by the definition of nu_train and with no theorem behind it. The Lean SCOPE ('not proved: Algorithm 1's Monte-Carlo estimator as an estimator of E_{nu_train} delta f_init') concerns identifying that nu_train with a named law, the occupation measure of the stopped samplers (through the hazard and p_t as survival probability). The text does not claim that. The text never says which nu_train the b condition refers to (finding 2). For the empirical nu-hat itself the norm is infinite on a continuous S. (3) l.436, 'the weak-FM term E_{s ~ nu_train} delta f_init(s) in (15)'. This is the penalty of Eq. (15) (l.384) and the term named at l.388. The control claimed is delta/(1 + delta) <= min(1, delta) <= N E_{nu_train} delta f_init for lambda <= N nu_train (EGF.negMass_ratio_le_min, EGF.integral_le_mul_of_le_smul; the loss form is the third conjunct of EGF.loss_controls_defect). It needs ||d lambda/d nu_train||_inf < infinity, which v2 states only through l.421 (finding 1). added_hypotheses = ['b >= 1 + ||d lambda / d nu_train||_inf ...'] is in the edited statement (l.421). The edit adds no other hypothesis: moving b to the penalty and the linear term are the change of loss itself. Kind gap, no refutation. EGF.SwapM.loss_lt_entropy (0 < b < log 2 breaks the floor, at N = 1) lies outside Algorithm 1's new range b >= 2. Eq. (15) at l.386 still allows it (finding 1). The applied text is C-35's corrected text verbatim. It writes eqref for (ref), renders the same, and adds ', and' to join the following 'with p_t'.

l.415, the buffer step's new parenthetical, clause by clause. (a) 'B<- holds paths of the sampler of the reversed generative flow (pi<-*, F_in*) started from kappa'. This is DEC-142's reading. The object is EGF.GenerativeFlow.reverse F B (policy B, outflow inflow F.policy F.outflow), a generative flow in v2's sense (l.161: a Markov kernel and a finite outflow). (b) 'the reversed flow is flow matching from kappa-hat to F-hat_init = F_init + delta F_init'. This is EGF.reverse_isFlowMatching_iff (T = Finit + inferenceDefect). It needs IsBackwardPolicy, which holds because pi<-* is the flow's backward policy (Appendix A, l.769-777). Existence on v2's Polish spaces (l.377) is EGF.reverse_sampling_posterior, with Mathlib's posterior; it also gives almost-sure stopping and s_tau ~ F-hat_init/(1 + delta), but the text does not use that. kappaHat = (F_init + F_in) - F_out and inferenceDefect = F_out - (F_init + F_in) are kappa-hat of Corollary 3.9 and Definition 3.7's delta F_init at F_term = kappa-hat. Its density is l.381's delta f_init, so F-hat_init has density f-hat_init. (c) 'its sampler continues at s_t with probability (1 + f-hat_init/f_in*)^{-1}(s_t), f-hat_init := f_init + delta f_init'. This is EGF.reverse_cont_ae_eq. For any Markov B, F_init << lambda a probability, F_out << lambda and InflowAC, cont = f_in/(f_init + delta f_init + f_in), (F-hat_init + F_in)-a.e. Where f_in > 0 that equals algBackwardFactorReversed = (1 + (f_init + delta f_init)/f_in)^{-1} (EGF.reverse_cont_ae_eq_backwardFactor), and where f_in = 0 it equals 0. The a.e. is the paper's own convention for the hazard (l.165 footnote, C-14: defined up to an (F_term + F_out)-null set). The continuation does not depend on the initial law, so 'started from kappa' instead of kappa-hat changes nothing. The text claims no law for the paths started from kappa, and in particular not that they are the time reversal of the forward paths (not proved: EGF/Loss.lean SCOPE). (d) 'as the forward sampler continues with probability (1 + f-hat_term/f_out*)^{-1}'. This is EGF.cont_kappaHat_ae_eq_forwardFactor, C-3's anchor. l.426, the backward factor of p_t, prod_{t'<t} (1 + (f-hat_init/f_in*)(s_t'))^{-1}, is EGF.algBackwardFactorReversed. The disclosed deviation keeps the corrected meaning. f-hat_init is defined as f_init + delta f_init at l.415, in an earlier STATE of the same algorithm, so it is defined before use. It clashes with no other symbol: it appears only at l.415 and l.426, and it is the density of v2's F-hat_init := F_init + delta F_init (l.330). Dropping displaystyle inside eqnarray* changes nothing in display math. Rebuilt with C-38's literal form, the alignment's Overfull hbox grows from 9.31795pt to 45.91176pt, as the corrector said. With the applied form it stays at 9.31795pt. C-3's applied sentence (l.429) stays true of the corrected factor. With f_init >= 0, delta f_init >= 0 and f_in* > 0, the factor is in (0,1] (EGF.algBackwardFactorReversed_eq, second conjunct). Its 'so that' still follows from the clause it follows. Refutation EGF.printed_reverse_not_isFlowMatching: the printed factor (1 + delta f_init/f_in)^{-1} is the continuation of the reversed flow toward delta F_init alone, which is not flow matching from kappa-hat (masses 1 + delta against delta). The edited factor is the continuation toward F-hat_init, for which the flow is flow matching. The refuting instance is no longer covered. added_hypotheses = [] is right. The f_in* > 0 qualification is C-3's (l.429), and the B<- reading is DEC-142's ruling, not a hypothesis. Register: `corrected` still gives the literal l.400 form, and `finding` cites stale v2 lines (finding 4).

findings.what: The hypothesis on nu_train is stated only inside Algorithm 1. l.436 (edited: 'the weak-FM term E_{nu_train} delta f_init in (15) controls delta/(1 + delta)') and l.458 (unchanged: 'the weak-FM term in (15) also controls the normalization factor', log(1 + delta) <= delta) hold for lambda <= N nu_train. Then delta/(1 + delta) <= min(1, delta) <= N E_{nu_train} delta f_init (EGF.integral_le_mul_of_le_smul, EGF.negMass_ratio_le_min, EGF.loss_controls_defect). They fail for an arbitrary nu_train, which l.386 allows ('for some training distribution of paths nu_train and b > 0'). With nu_train = delta_true in the SwapM instance, delta f_init(true) = 0, so E_{nu_train} delta f_init = 0 while delta = m. v2 supplies ||d lambda/d nu_train||_inf < infinity only through Algorithm 1's b >= 1 + ||d lambda/d nu_train||_inf (l.421), two lines above l.436. That is why this finding is minor and not an overclaim. The same holds of the informal 'controls' of l.458, which is v1 text. On the corrector's l.386 flag: real, but not an error. 'b > 0' is a correct range for the definition (15), and DEC-143 leaves Eq. (15) unchanged. Algorithm 1 now takes a sub-range, which is consistent. But the loss has no floor for 0 < b < log 2 (EGF.SwapM.loss_lt_entropy), so the control the discussion motivates needs Algorithm 1's range. It belongs to C-35, whose `printed` already lists v1 l.364-366, and DEC-143 names the condition 'for the control of the sampling error'. It is not a new entry. C-35's `summary` ('b large enough for the control of the sampling error') reads as if Eq. (15) itself now said so.

findings.what: 'A Monte-Carlo estimate of (15)' is true by construction and claims no more than the Lean (see C-35's notes). But the text never says which nu_train it means, and the b condition is stated against that unnamed nu_train. For the empirical buffer measure the norm is infinite. The display also inherits two notational gaps from v1 l.395, so it reads as an estimate only through an implicit convention. There is no sum over the buffer's trajectories (the 1/(2B) normalizes a sum over a single path s), and the sum runs to tau while the trajectories run to t_max. These gaps predate the batch. The new phrase makes them visible.
findings.fix: For the planner, as a typo entry or a C-35 round 2: write sum_{s in B} sum_{t=1}^{t_max} (or say what tau is). Name nu_train, e.g. '... of (15) for nu_train the law of the buffer's states weighted by p_t'. Do not identify it with the samplers' occupation measure: that needs the survival identity for p_t, which is not proved (EGF/Loss.lean SCOPE).

findings.what: The condition b >= 1 + ||d lambda/d nu_train||_inf appears without its reason. The bound it buys is nowhere stated in v2: the floor H(kappa) <= L, and TV(s_tau || kappa) <= (1/sqrt 2) sqrt(L - H(kappa)) + min(1, ||d lambda/d nu_train||_inf (L - H(kappa))) for a finite L (EGF.loss_controls_sampling_essSup, the follow-up's il_tv_bound at q = 1). The corollary that would carry it is commented out (v2 l.363-371). DEC-143 and the marker say 'for the control of the sampling error', but the rendered text does not. This claims less than the Lean, not more.

findings.what: Real, but it belongs to the experiments batch, not to this one. 'Our EGF is trained using the KL-weakFM loss together with a regularization R' (and the abstract's 'using the KL-weakFM loss') named Eq. (15) in v1 as well (v1 l.362: 'The KL-weakFM loss can then be defined as follows'). Eq. (15) is unchanged, and Algorithm 1 is never referenced, so no changed symbol is left inconsistent. What the batch changes is that v2's IL algorithm (b on the linear penalty, b >= 1 + N, the backward factor with f-hat_init) may no longer be the procedure behind the reported numbers. The reported runs may have used v1's printed Algorithm 1 (b on the cross-entropy, the printed backward factor) or the squared penalty of v1 l.407 ('WeakFMPower' 2.0 in the TensorFlow configurations). The loss trained also adds R, with an unstated weight. Only the author or the reproduction can supply that fact. It is not a reading of the mathematics.

answers.monte_carlo: Not an overclaim. Eq. (15) leaves nu_train free, so L estimates (15) for nu_train := E[p_t-weighted buffer state measure] by definition. The unproved item of the Lean SCOPE is the identification of that nu_train with the stopped samplers' occupation measure, and the text does not assert it. The weakness is that nu_train is unnamed (finding 2).
answers.implicit_hypotheses: hnuT (lambda << nu_train) is presupposed by the paper's own convention for Radon-Nikodym derivatives (l.157). hM (essSup finite) is forced by a real b >= 1 + ||.||_inf. Neither is an unstated hypothesis in the sense of an overclaim. They are worth naming once at l.386 (finding 1) and in C-35's `added_hypotheses` (finding 4c).
answers.C3_sentence: Still true (l.429). With the corrected factor, each backward factor is f_in/(f_init + delta f_init + f_in), in (0,1] where f_in* > 0 (EGF.algBackwardFactorReversed_eq).
answers.l386: Real as a gap, not as an error. 'b > 0' is a valid range for the definition, and Algorithm 1's b >= 1 + N is a consistent sub-range. But l.436 and l.458 need lambda <= N nu_train, and the loss has no floor for small b (EGF.SwapM.loss_lt_entropy). It belongs to C-35 (round 2; C-35 already prints v1 l.364-366), not to a new entry (finding 1).
